body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py:427-431`, `inherit()` fills empty metadata fields from the parent sidecar using direct reference assignment `meta[field] = parent_value`. When parent fields contain mutable containers such as dictionaries or lists (for example `artist`, `holder`, `site`, or `rights`), in-place modifications to the child sidecar mutate the parent sidecar object in memory.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`
- `tests/test_variants.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: shallow copying dictionary references without deep copying nested mutable data structures is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter the list of inheritable fields or stable identifier merge rules.

## Tasks
- [ ] Deep copy inherited metadata values in `inherit()` within `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py` using `copy.deepcopy(parent_value)`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_variants.py` asserting mutating child metadata fields does not alter parent sidecar dictionaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_variants.py` passes with 100% success.
- Creating a child variant with `inherit(parent_meta, child_meta)` and mutating `child_meta["artist"]["name"]` leaves `parent_meta["artist"]["name"]` unchanged.
- Deliberate break: change `copy.deepcopy(parent_value)` back to `parent_value` in `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`, run `pytest tests/test_variants.py`, and verify that the mutation independence test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Import `copy` and use `copy.deepcopy` when assigning inheritable fields in `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`.
title: fix(identity): deepcopy mutable metadata values during variant inheritance
